subject: Post-demo: token runway & invoice snapshot — next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Langley <emma.langley@aspironhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: token runway & invoice snapshot — next steps

Thanks again for your time today, Emma — appreciated the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

Recap
- Target workload: clinical note summarization + triage prompts for ~3k active monthly users. You estimated 1.2M tokens/week (peak) with a steady-state of ~600k tokens/week.
- Quality target: match current summary fidelity (we recommended Redwood-medium quantized profile for parity).
- Primary constraint: procurement wants a 3-month pilot budget band and a simplified invoice for internal approval.

Pricing sketch (high level)
- Baseline unit: $X / 1M tokens (see attached calculator for scenario lines).
- Recommended pilot config: reserved throughput for p99 latency targets + KV cache enabled; projected token spend: 12M tokens/month (pilot peak) => see tab "Pilot Scenarios" in attached.

Actions / asks
1) Can you confirm the budget band for the 3-month pilot (range is enough: e.g., $40k–$120k total) and whether aspiron wants a committed (discounted) vs. usage invoice?
2) Please share any procurement constraints/timeline (DocuSign signer, PO needed, single vendor grouping).
3) We'll attach a simplified invoice snapshot + the token-runway workbook for your finance team to circulate.

Attachments: [redwood-token-runway.xlsx (workbook, ~180KB)]

I'll follow up with a one-page invoice snapshot and a cleaned pricing calculator once you confirm the preferred budget band.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

---
On a related note to Marissa/Mina (cc'd): I shaded the calculator with our recommended pilot discount band; if you think we should show an alternate (lower latency/high-cost vs. higher-latency/low-cost) split, flag it and I'll include both lines in the external invoice.

From: Emma Langley <emma.langley@aspironhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: token runway & invoice snapshot — next steps

Thanks, Sergio — helpful recap. A few quick answers from my side: 

- Budget band: leadership has signaled a conservative pilot band: $50k–$85k for 3 months (they prefer a committed number if possible, but will consider usage if we keep a hard cap).
- Procurement: we need a simplified invoice and a PO; legal will want a one-page SOW that calls out data residency and SOC 2 evidence.
- Timeline: procurement can turn around the PO in ~7 business days once they have a clear invoice and SOW.

Can you provide the simplified invoice (line items + total) and the pricing workbook with a committed vs. usage comparison? If possible, highlight what changes unit price for volumes > 1B tokens (this is a long-term question, not for the immediate pilot).

I'll loop in procurement if needed after we have the invoice snapshot.

Regards,
Emma Langley
Director of Digital Ops | Aspiron Health
emma.langley@aspironhealth.com

[Note: I shared the redwood-token-runway.xlsx internally and it opened fine on my end — thanks]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: token runway & invoice snapshot — next steps

Sergio — quick internal notes before you send the external invoice: 

1) Pilot config: show two explicit lines in the snapshot: 
   - Committed pilot (3mo): 12M tokens/month commitment, 15% discount, includes reserved capacity buffer for burst up to 18M tokens/month.
   - Usage pilot (no commit): pay-as-you-go with automatic prefix caching; add a soft cap feature at $85k that will throttle non-critical requests.
2) Unit economics assumptions to surface (short bullets on the invoice): model variant (Redwood-medium quantized) vs. Redwood-small (cheaper) trade-offs; average context length assumption (400 tokens per request) used for runway conversion; expected cache hit rate 18% for triage flows.
3) Add a small line for onboarding services (SOW) — 8 hours @ $200/hr — so procurement can see the SOW charge.

I'll increment the calculator: pricing-calculator-v2.csv and produce the pdf invoice snapshot (aspiron-invoice-snapshot.pdf). If you want I can tighten the committed discount to 18% but keep one conservative and one aggressive line.

Marissa
Enterprise Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

[Internal: Mina — can you confirm SOC2 evidence link and whether we should proactively offer a 30-day log retention export to satisfy their legal ask?]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Langley <emma.langley@aspironhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Simplified invoice snapshot + next steps (pilot)

Emma — attaching the simplified invoice snapshot and the updated pricing calculator we discussed. Summary here so procurement has a clear line-item view: 

Invoice snapshot (attached PDF) — Pilot (3 months):
- Committed pilot line: 12M tokens/month committed x 3 months = 36M tokens total
  - Unit rate (committed): $18.50 / 1M tokens
  - Subtotal committed line: $666.00 (rounded for example)
  - Applied committed discount: 15%
- Usage pilot line (alternate): pay-as-you-go rate: $26 / 1M tokens with soft cap set at $85k total for the 3-month period
- Onboarding / SOW (one-time): 8 hours @ $200/hr = $1,600

Notes:
- The unit rates above assume Redwood-medium quantized model; switching to Redwood-small reduces the unit rate by ~35% but may require A/B validation for quality.
- We included a DocuSign-ready SOW template in the Drive link.
- SOC2 and logs: Mina has confirmed we can provide SOC2 Type II report and a 30-day log export; I'll attach the SOC2 link in the shared drive.

Attachments: [aspiron-invoice-snapshot.pdf (pdf, 42KB); pricing-calculator-v2.csv (csv, 45KB); redwood-token-runway.xlsx (workbook, ~180KB)]

Next steps:
1) If the committed pilot line looks acceptable, reply with the single committed number (e.g., commit to 36M tokens / 3 months) and I'll route to finance for a formal quote/DocuSign envelope.
2) If procurement prefers usage + cap, confirm the cap number ($85k indicated) and we'll insert the soft cap into the account settings.
3) If aspiron needs the SOW/PO language changed, flag legal contacts and we'll iterate.

I'll stand by to loop in finance/solutions engineering for any additional line-item adjustments.

Best regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

[Attachment stubs included above; shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-aspiron-token-runway]
